title: Vaccines: Historical Development
text: The concept of vaccination was pioneered by Edward Jenner in 1796, when he demonstrated that inoculation with cowpox virus protected against smallpox. Louis Pasteur developed the germ theory of disease and created vaccines for chicken cholera, anthrax, and rabies in the 1880s. The 20th century saw vaccines developed for diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, polio, measles, mumps, and rubella. The smallpox vaccine led to the global eradication of smallpox, declared by the WHO in 1980. Polio has been eliminated from most of the world through mass vaccination campaigns. The hepatitis B vaccine was the first vaccine developed to prevent cancer.
